907.text:
Assertion : In some cases oxygen shows positive oxidation number though it is an electronegative element.
Reason : Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
907.sol:
Oxygen is the most electronegative element after fluorine. Therefore, in the compounds between oxygen and fluorine, oxygen is found to show positive oxidation state.
e.g. $\mathrm{OF}_2$ : Oxygen difluoride.
Oxidation state of oxygen here is +2 .

2776.text:

Assertion (A): Ionic compounds are formed by nondirectional bonds
Reasoning (R): They are soluble in nonpolar solvents The correct answer is

Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of $(A)$

2776.sol:
Ionic bonds are electrostatic forces of attraction that are non-directional in nature.

Hence, the following effect is known as Electromeric& effect.

5447.text: If two gases $\mathrm{CH}_4$ and $\mathrm{SO}_2$, are allowed to enter from the two ends of a $1 \mathrm{ km}$ long vacuum tube at the same time, where will the gases meet from the $\mathrm{CH}_4$ end?

$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{CH}_4}=16 ;\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{CH}_4}\right)_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{RT}}{16}}=\frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}}}{4} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{SO}_2}=$64 ;$\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{SO}_2}\right)_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{RT}}{64}}=\frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}}}{8} \mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$\\
& \therefore$\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{CH}_4}\right)_{\mathrm{rms}}$>$\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{SO}_2}\right)_{\mathrm{rms}}
\end{aligned}$Suppose, at time ' $\mathrm{t}$ ', both the gas will meet.
At time $\mathrm{t}, \mathrm{CH}_4$ molecules travel $\frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}}}{4} \mathrm{tm}$ and At time $\mathrm{SO}_2$ molecules travel $\frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}}}{8} \mathrm{tm}$.
$\therefore \frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}} \mathrm{t}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}} \mathrm{t}}{8}=1000$ or $\frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}} \mathrm{t}}{4}\left(1+\frac{1}{2}\right)=1000
or \frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}} \mathrm{t}}{4} \times \frac{3}{2}=1000
or \quad t=\frac{8000}{3 \sqrt{3 R T}}\therefore$ Distance travelled by time ' $\mathrm{t}$ '

=$\frac{\sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}}}{4} \times \frac{8000}{3 \sqrt{3 \mathrm{RT}}}=$667 $\mathrm{~m}$

It is given that, a spherical iron ball$ of 10$ cm radius is coated with a layer of ice of uniform thickness, let the thickness is '$x$' $cm$, then volume of the ball is~$V = $\dfrac{4}{3}$\pi$\left(10 + x\right)$3cm^{3} .

On differentiating w.r.t. ' $t$', we get

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi\left(10 + x\right)2\dfrac{dx}{dt}$~ & $. . . ( i )$

where $t$ is time in $min$.

It is given, the $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = - 50{cm}^{3} / min,$~when $x$ is $5$ cm, then

$- 50 = 4\pi\left(10 + 5\right)2\dfrac{dx}{dt}$~ [from Eq. $( i )$]

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = - \dfrac{50}{4\pi\left(225\right)} = - \dfrac{1}{18\pi}cm / min .

Negative sign indicates$ the thickness of ice layer decreases with time.

Thus, the~thickness of ice layer decreases at a rate&$\dfrac{1}{18\pi}$cm / min .

Hence, option $\left(D\right)$& is correct.

6480.text: If $\frac{x+1}{(2 x-1)(3 x+1)}=\frac{A}{2 x-1}+\frac{B}{3 x+1}$, then $16 A+9 B$ is equal to
6480.sol:
$\begin{gathered}
\frac{x+1}{(2 x-1)(3 x+1)}=\frac{A}{2 x-1}+\frac{B}{3 x+1} \\
x+1=A(3 x+1)+B(2 x-1)
\end{gathered}$
Put,
$x=\frac{1}{2} \text{$ in $Eq. }\begin{aligned}
& \frac{3}{2}=A\left(3 \cdot \frac{1}{2}+1\right)+B(0) \\
& \frac{3}{2}=A \cdot \frac{5}{2} \Rightarrow A=\frac{3}{5}
\end{aligned}$
Put,
$\begin{aligned}
& x=-\frac{1}{3} \text{$ in $Eq. (i) } \\
& \frac{2}{3}=A(0)+B\left(2 \cdot\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)-1\right) \\
& \frac{2}{3}=B\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) \Rightarrow B=-\frac{2}{5}
\end{aligned}$
Consider
$16 A+9 B=16\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)+9\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right)=6$
Hence, option (3) is correct.

Let $\quad z=x+i y \begin{aligned}& \therefore \quad(x+i y)^3+x-i y=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x³+(i y)^3+3 x² i y+3 x(i y)^2+x-i y=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x³-y³ i+3 x² y i-3 x y²+x-i y=0 \\
& \Rightarrow\left(x^3-3 x y²+x\right)+\left(-y^3+3 x² y-y\right) i=0
\end{aligned}

On equating real$ and $imaginary parts, we get

\begin{aligned}& x³-3 x y²+x=0 \\
& \text{ or } \quad-y^3+3 x² y-y=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x\left(x^2-3 y²+1\right)=0 \\
& \text{ or } \quad-y\left(y^2-3 x²+1\right)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x=0 \text{ and }x^2-3 y²+1=0 \\
& \text{ or }y=0 \text{ and }y^2-3 x²+1=0 \\
& \text{ Now, }\\
& x³-3 y²+1=y²-3 x²+1 \\
& 4 x²=4 y² \\
& x= \pmy \\
& y²-3 y²+1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 y²=1 \Rightarrow y= \pm \frac{1}{2}\\
& \Rightarrow \quad x= \pm \frac{1}{2}\\
&
\end{aligned}

Hence, their solutions are$(0,0) and $\left( \pm \frac{1}{2}, \pm \frac{1}{2}\right)$
Hence, number of solutions is 5 .

7955.text:
Let $a, b, c$ be such that $( b + c ) \ne 0$ and

$\left|\begin{cases}a & a + 1 & a - 1 \\ - b & b + 1 & b - 1 \\ c & c - 1 & c + 1\end{cases}\right|+ \left|\begin{cases}a + 1 & b + 1 & c - 1 \\ a - 1 & b - 1 & c + 1 \\ \left(- 1\right)n + 2a & \left(- 1\right)n - 1b & \left(- 1\right)nc\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Then the value of $n$ is
7955.sol:
$\left|\begin{cases}a & a + 1 & a - 1 \\ - b & b + 1 & b - 1 \\ c & c - 1 & c + 1\end{cases}\right| + \left|\begin{cases}a + 1 & b + 1 & c - 1 \\ a - 1 & b - 1 & c + 1 \\ \left(- 1\right)n + 2a & \left(- 1\right)n - 1b & \left(- 1\right)nc\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a & a + 1 & a - 1 \\ - b & b + 1 & b - 1 \\ c & c - 1 & c + 1\end{cases}\right| + \left(- 1\right)n\left|\begin{cases}a + 1 & b + 1 & c - 1 \\ a - 1 & b - 1 & c + 1 \\ a & - b & c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a & a + 1 & a - 1 \\ - b & b + 1 & b - 1 \\ c & c - 1 & c + 1\end{cases}\right| + \left(- 1\right)n\left|\begin{cases}a + 1 & a - 1 & a \\ b + 1 & b - 1 & - b \\ c - 1 & c + 1 & c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a & a + 1 & a - 1 \\ - b & b + 1 & b - 1 \\ c & c - 1 & c + 1\end{cases}\right| + \left(- 1\right)n\left|\begin{cases}a & a + 1 & a - 1 \\ - b & b + 1 & b - 1 \\ c & c - 1 & c + 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ ( 1 + \left(- 1\right)n ) \left|\begin{cases}a & a + 1 & a - 1 \\ - b & b + 1 & b - 1 \\ c & c - 1 & c + 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Hence,~$n$ is an odd integer.

13649.text: A hydrogen like atom has one electron revolving round a stationary nucleus. If the energy required to excite the electron from the 2 nd orbital to 3 rd orbit is \(47.2 $\mathrm{eV}$\), find the atomic number of the given atom.
13649.sol:
The energy of \(n\)th orbit is given as
\(E_n=\frac{-R h C z^2}{n^2}\)
For hydrogen atom, \(z=1\) and \(n=1\), hence
\(E_1=\frac{-R h C \cdot 1^2}{1^2}=-R h C\)
We know that, \(R h C=13.6 \mathrm{eV}\)
\(\therefore \quad E_1=-13.6 \mathrm{eV}\)
For \(n=2\),
\begin{aligned}& E_2=$\frac{-R h C z²}{2^2}=\frac{-13.6 z²}{4}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad & E_2=$\frac{-13.6 z²}{4}$\quad \ldots ( i)
\end{aligned} \)
Similarly,$ for $\(n=3\),
\(E_3=\frac{-13.6}{9}z^2 \quad \ldots (ii)\)
Given,$\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow& \frac{-13.6}{9} z^2-\left(\frac{-13.6 z^2}{4}\right)=47.2 \\
\Rightarrow & 13.6 \times \frac{5}{36} z^2=47.2 \\
\Rightarrow & z²=24.98 \\
\Rightarrow & z² \simeq 25 \\
\Rightarrow & z=5
\end{array}$

13810.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
13810.text: A shell of mass $m$ moving with velocity $v$ suddenly breaks into two pieces. If one of those parts having mass $m / 6$ remains stationary, find the velocity of the other part.
13810.sol:
Given that, mass of shell $=m$
Mass of lst part, $m_1=\frac{m}{6}$
Then, mass of 2nd part, $m_2=m-\frac{m}{6}=\frac{5 m}{6}$
Velocity of lst part, $v_1=0$
Velocity of shell $=v$
Let velocity of 2nd part $=v_2$
By using law of conservation of linear momentum,
Initial linear momentum $=$ final linear momentum.
$m v=m_1 v_1+m_2 v_2$
Substituting the values, we get
$m v=\frac{m}{6} \times 0+\frac{5 m}{6} \times v_2\Rightarrow \quad v_2=\frac{6}{5} v$
Hence, the velocity of 2 nd part is $\frac{6}{5} v$ in the same direction as that of shell.

(i) and (ii), we get \(\therefore \quad T-m_1 g+m_2 g-T=m_1 a+m_2 a\) \(m_2 g-m_1 g=a\left(m_1+m_2\right)\) or \(a=\frac{\left(m_2-m_1\right) g}{\left(m_1+m_2\right)}\) Hence, acceleration, \(a=\left(\frac{m_2-m_1}{m_1+m_2}\right) g\) \(\therefore\) Acceleration, \(a=\frac{(0.72-0.36)}{1.08} \times 10\) \(a=\frac{3.6}{1.08} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \quad \ldots (iii)\) Now, the tension force in the string is, for block 1st, \(m_1=0.36\) \(\begin{aligned} & T-m_1 g=m_1 a \\ & \frac{T-m_1 g}{m_1}=a \\ & \frac{T-3.6}{0.36}=\frac{3.6}{1.08} \\ & T=3.6+0.36 \times \frac{3.6}{1.08} \\ & T=4.8 \quad \ldots (iv) \end{aligned}\) Distance travelled by mass \(m_1\) block, By displacement-time relation, Displacement, \(s=u t+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{at}^2\) \([\because u=0]\) [by kinetic equation for uniformly motion] \(s=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3.6}{1.08} \times(1)^2 \quad[\therefore t=1\) second given] \(s=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3.6}{1.08}\)...(v) Now, work done by the string on the block of mass \(\left(m_1\right)\) is \(0.36 \mathrm{~kg}\). \(\therefore\) Work done, \(W=\) Tension force \((T) \times\) displacement \((s)\) \(W=T \times \frac{1}{2} a t^2\) From Eqs. (iv) and (v), we get \(\begin{aligned} & W=4.8 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3.6}{1.08} \\ & W=\frac{16}{2} \Rightarrow W=8 \mathrm{~J} \end{aligned}\)

20227.subject: Chemistry
20227.text: Which of the following is the most stable free radical?
20227.sol:
The stability of free radicals is determined by factors such as resonance, hyperconjugation, and inductive effects.

Option (1) is a vinyl radical, which is highly unstable due to the $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atom having the unpaired electron in an $sp^2$ orbital.

Option (2) is a methyl radical, which has no alkyl groups to provide stability through hyperconjugation.

Option (3) is a tertiary butyl radical, which is stabilized by hyperconjugation from nine $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms.

Option (4) is a diphenylmethyl radical, which is highly stabilized by extensive resonance with two phenyl rings. The unpaired electron is delocalized over the entire conjugated system of both benzene rings, making it significantly more stable than the tertiary butyl radical.

Answer: $\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5\right)_2 \dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}$

20452.text: What volume of $0.2 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ needs to be added to $100 \mathrm{ml}$ of $0.4 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COONa}^2$ solution to prepare a buffer of pH equal to 4.91 ? ($\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ is 4.76)
20452.sol:
The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer is given by:

$\text{pH} = \text{pK}_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)

Given \text{pH} =4.91$, $\text{pK}_{a} =$$4.76$, and the concentration of salt $[\text{CH}_{3}\text{COONa}] =0.4 \text{ M} with volume $ V_{s} = 100 $\text{ ml}$.

Substituting the values into the equation:

4.91 = 4.76 + $\log\left( \dfrac{n_{$$\text{salt}$$}}{n_{$$\text{acid}$$}} \right)

0.15 = \log$\left( \dfrac{0.4 \times 100}{0.2 \times V_{a}} \right)$

Taking the antilog of both sides:

10^{0.15} = \dfrac{40}{0.2 \times V_{a}}

1.4125 = \dfrac{40}{0.2 \times V_{a}}

0.2 \times$ V_{a} = $\dfrac{40}{1.4125}$$

0.2 \times$ V_{a} = 28.3186$

$V_{a} = $\dfrac{28.3186}{0.2} =$141.59 $\text{ ml}$

Answer: 141.59 ml

20491.subject: Chemistry
20491.text: Which among the following is NOT in accordance with the property stated against it?
options: $HI > HBr > HCl > HF$ [Acidic Property in Water]
20491.sol:
The oxidising power of halogens decreases down the group: $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$.

The acidic strength of hydrogen halides in water increases down the group due to a decrease in bond dissociation enthalpy: $HI > HBr > HCl > HF$.

Electronegativity decreases down the group: $F > Cl > Br > I$.

The bond dissociation energy of halogens does not follow a regular trend. Due to strong interelectronic repulsions between the lone pairs on the small fluorine atoms, the $F-F$ bond is weaker than the $Cl-Cl$ and $Br-Br$ bonds. The correct order of bond dissociation energy is $Cl_2 > Br_2 > F_2 > I_2$.

Thus, the order $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$ for bond dissociation energy is incorrect.

Answer: $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$ [Bond Dissociation Energy]

21552.sol:
Let $\dfrac{1}{(x+2)(x^2+1)} = \dfrac{A}{x+2} + \dfrac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}$.

Multiplying both sides by $(x+2)(x^2+1)$, we get $1 = A(x^2+1) + (Bx+C)(x+2)$.

Setting $x = -2$, we get $1 = A(4+1) + 0$, which implies $5A = 1$, so $A = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Comparing coefficients of $x^2$, we get $A + B = 0$, so $B = -A = -\dfrac{1}{5}$.

Comparing constant terms, we get $A + 2C = 1$, so $\dfrac{1}{5} + 2C = 1$, which implies $2C = \dfrac{4}{5}$, so $C = \dfrac{2}{5}$.

The integral becomes $\int \left( \dfrac{1/5}{x+2} + \dfrac{-x/5 + 2/5}{x^2+1} \right) dx = \dfrac{1}{5} \int \dfrac{dx}{x+2} - \dfrac{1}{10} \int \dfrac{2x}{x^2+1} dx + \dfrac{2}{5} \int \dfrac{dx}{x^2+1}$.

This evaluates to $\dfrac{1}{5} \log |x+2| - \dfrac{1}{10} \log |x^2+1| + \dfrac{2}{5} \tan^{-1} x + c$.

Comparing with $p \log |x+2| + q \log |x^2+1| + r \tan^{-1} x + c$, we have $p = \dfrac{1}{5}$, $q = -\dfrac{1}{10}$, and $r = \dfrac{2}{5}$.

Therefore, $p + q + r = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{2 - 1 + 4}{10} = \dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

22186.text: The measure of the angle between the lines $x=k+1, \quad y=2 k-1, \quad z=2 k+3, \quad k \in \mathbb{R} \quad$ and $\quad \dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{1}=\dfrac{z-1}{-2}$ is
22186.sol:
The first line is given by $x = k+1$, $y = 2k-1$, $z = 2k+3$. This can be written in symmetric form as $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y+1}{2} = \dfrac{z-3}{2} = k$. The direction vector of this line is $\vec{v_1} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

The second line is given by $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{1} = \dfrac{z-1}{-2}$. The direction vector of this line is $\vec{v_2} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$.

The angle $\theta$ between the two lines is given by $\cos \theta = \dfrac{|\vec{v_1} \cdot \vec{v_2}|}{|\vec{v_1}| |\vec{v_2}|}$.

Calculating the dot product: $\vec{v_1} \cdot \vec{v_2} = (1)(2) + (2)(1) + (2)(-2) = 2 + 2 - 4 = 0$.

Since the dot product is $0$, the lines are perpendicular to each other. Therefore, the angle between the lines is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

22318.subject: Mathematics
22318.text: If the vectors $\mathrm{a}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{k}} ; \mathrm{b}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $\mathrm{c}=m \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ are coplanar, then the value of $m$ is
22318.sol:
Three vectors $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, and $\vec{c}$ are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product is zero, which is given by the determinant of the matrix formed by their components.

The condition is $\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) = 0$, which implies:

$\begin{vmatrix} 2 \text{ and } -3 \text{ and } 4 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } -1 \\ m \text{ and } -1 \text{ and } 2 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$2(2 \times 2 - (-1) \times (-1)) - (-3)(1 \times 2 - (-1) \times m) + 4(1 \times (-1) - 2 \times m) = 0$

$2(4 - 1) + 3(2 + m) + 4(-1 - 2m) = 0$

$2(3) + 6 + 3m - 4 - 8m = 0$

$6 + 6 + 3m - 4 - 8m = 0$

$8 - 5m = 0$

$5m = 8$

$m = \dfrac{8}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{8}{5}$

22952.subject: Physics
22952.text: The molecules of a given mass of a gas have root mean square speed of $120 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ at $88^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and 1 atmospheric pressure. The root mean square speed of the molecules at $127^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and 2 atmospheric pressure is
22952.sol:
The root mean square speed $v_{rms}$ of gas molecules is given by the formula $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$.

From this formula, it is evident that $v_{rms}$ depends only on the temperature $T$ and the molar mass $M$ of the gas. It is independent of the pressure $P$ of the gas.

Given $v_{rms,1} = 120 \text{ m/s}$ at $T_1 = 88^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C} = 88 + 273 = 361 \text{ K}$.

We need to find $v_{rms,2}$ at $T_2 = 127^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C} = 127 + 273 = 400 \text{ K}$.

Taking the ratio of the two speeds:

$\dfrac{v_{rms,2}}{v_{rms,1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}}$

Substituting the values:

$\dfrac{v_{rms,2}}{120} = \sqrt{\dfrac{400}{361}}$

$\dfrac{v_{rms,2}}{120} = \dfrac{20}{19}$

$v_{rms,2} = 120 \times \dfrac{20}{19} = \dfrac{2400}{19} \approx 126.315 \text{ m/s}$.

Answer: 126.3 m/s

23437.text: A record player is spinning at an angular velocity of $45 \mathrm{ rpm}$ just before it is turned off. It then decelerates at a constant rate of $0.8 \mathrm{ rad} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$. The angular displacement is
23437.sol:
The initial angular velocity $\omega_0$ is given as $45 \text{ rpm}$. Converting this to $\text{rad s}^{-1}$:

$\omega_0 = 45 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} \text{ rad s}^{-1} = \dfrac{45 \times 2\pi}{60} \text{ rad s}^{-1} = 1.5\pi \text{ rad s}^{-1} \approx 4.712 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

The deceleration $\alpha$ is $0.8 \text{ rad s}^{-2}$. Since it is decelerating, $\alpha = -0.8 \text{ rad s}^{-2}$. The final angular velocity $\omega$ when the record player stops is $0 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

Using the kinematic equation $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angular displacement:

$0 = (1.5\pi)^2 + 2(-0.8)\theta$

$1.6\theta = (1.5\pi)^2$

$1.6\theta = 2.25 \times \pi^2$

Taking $\pi^2 \approx 9.8696$:

$1.6\theta = 2.25 \times 9.8696 = 22.2066$

$\theta = \dfrac{22.2066}{1.6} = 13.879 \text{ rad} \approx 13.88 \text{ rad}$.

Answer: 13.88 rad

Let $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_n$ be mutually exclusive events with $P\left(H_i\right)>0, i=1,2, \ldots, n$. Let $E$ be any other event with $0 < P(E) < 1$.
Statement I $P\left(H_i / E\right)>P\left(E / H_i\right) P\left(H_i\right)$ for $i=1,2, \ldots, n$.
Statement II $\sum_{i=1}^n P\left(H_i\right)=1$
options:
Statement I is true, Statement II is true; Statement II is a correct explanation for Statement I

Statement I is true, Statement II is true; Statement II is not a correct explanation for Statement II

Statement I is true, Statement II is false

Statement I is false, Statement II is true
25772.sol:
Statement : I If $P\left(H_i \cap E\right)=0$ for some $i$, then

P$\left(\frac{H_i}{E}\right)=$P$\left(\frac{E}{H_i}\right)=$0

If $P\left(H_i \cap E\right) \neq 0$ for $\forall i=1,2, \ldots . n$, then

$\begin{aligned}$P$\left(\frac{H_i}{E}\right)$& =$\frac{P\left(H_i \cap E\right)}{P\left(H_i\right)} \times \frac{P\left(H_i\right)}{P(E)}$\\
& $\left.=\frac{P\left(\frac{E}{H_i}\right) \times P\left(H_i\right)}{P(E)}$>P$\left(\frac{E}{H_i}\right) \cdot$P$\left(H_i\right) \quad \text{ [as }0$< P(E) < 1\right]
\end{aligned}

Hence, Statement I may not always be true.
Statement II
Clearly, $H_1 \cup H_2 \cup \ldots . \cup H_n=S$ (sample space)

\Rightarrow \quad P$\left(H_1\right)$+P$\left(H_2\right)$+\ldots+P$\left(H_n\right)$=1 .

Hence, Statement II is true.

28136.text:
If the half life of a first order reaction is $6.93$ minutes then the time required for completion of $99$% of the reaction will be _____ minutes.
(Given : $\log 2 = 0.3010$)
28136.sol:
For a first-order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by:

$k = \dfrac{2.303 \log 2}{t_{1/2}}$

Using the standard approximation $2.303 \log 2 \approx 0.693$:

$k = \dfrac{0.693}{6.93} = 0.1 \text{ min}^{-1}$

The time required for $99\%$ completion of the reaction is given by the integrated rate law:

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a - x} \right)$

Here, the initial concentration $a = 100$ and the amount reacted $x = 99$, so $a - x = 1$.

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{0.1} \log \left( \dfrac{100}{1} \right)$

$t = 23.03 \times \log(10^2)$

$t = 23.03 \times 2 = 46.06 \text{ minutes}$

Answer: $46.06$

32841.text: If ${a}_{\alpha}$ is the greatest term in the sequence ${a}_{n} = \dfrac{{n}^{3}}{{n}^{4} + 147}, n = 1, 2, 3 . . . . ,$ then $\alpha$ is equal to $______$
32841.sol:
Let,

$y = \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4} + 147} = f\left(x\right)$

We know that, for increasing function $\dfrac{dy}{dx} > 0$

So, differentiating the given function $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4} + 147}$ we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- {x}^{2}\left({x}^{4} - 441\right)}{( {x}^{4} + 147{)}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- {x}^{2}\left({x}^{4} - 441\right)}{( {x}^{4} + 147{)}^{2}} > 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}\left({x}^{4} - 441\right)}{( {x}^{4} + 147{)}^{2}} < 0$

$⇒ {x}^{4} < 441$

Now for maxima/minima $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{4} = 441$

$⇒ x = \alpha, 4 < \alpha < 5$

$⇒$Maximum value of $f\left(x\right)$ is at $x = 4$ or $x = 5$

$f\left(4\right) = \dfrac{64}{403}, f\left(5\right) = \dfrac{125}{772}$

$∵ f\left(5\right) > f\left(4\right)$

$⇒ \alpha = 5$

34128.subject: Mathematics
34128.text: The value of the integral $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \left(\dfrac{4 - \csc^2 x}{\cos^4 x}\right) dx$ is:
34128.sol:
The given integral is $I = \displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \left(\dfrac{4 - \csc^2 x}{\cos^4 x}\right) dx$.

We can rewrite the integrand in terms of $\tan x and \sec x$. Using the identity $\csc^2 x = 1 + \cot^2 x = 1 + \dfrac{1}{\tan^2 x}$, we get:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \left(4 - 1 - \dfrac{1}{\tan^2 x}\right) \sec^4 x \, dx$

$I = \displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \left(3 - \dfrac{1}{\tan^2 x}\right) (1 + \tan^2 x) \sec^2 x \, dx$

Substitute $t = \tan x$, which gives $dt = \sec^2 x \, dx$.

The limits of integration change as follows:
When $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $t = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.
When $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, $t = \sqrt{3}$.

The integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{1/\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}} \left(3 - \dfrac{1}{t^2}\right) (1 + t^2) dt$

Expanding the integrand, we get:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{1/\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}} \left(3 + 3t^2 - \dfrac{1}{t^2} - 1\right) dt$

$I = \displaystyle\int_{1/\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}} \left(3t^2 + 2 - t^{-2}\right) dt$

Integrating with respect to $t$:

$I = \left[ t^3 + 2t + \dfrac{1}{t} \right]_{1/\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}}$

Substitute the upper limit $t = \sqrt{3}$:

$\left( \sqrt{3} \right)^3 + 2\sqrt{3} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = 3\sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{3} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \dfrac{16\sqrt{3}}{3} = \dfrac{48}{3\sqrt{3}}$

Substitute the lower limit $t = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$:

$\left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \right)^3 + 2\left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \right) + \sqrt{3} = \dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{3}} + \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} + \sqrt{3} = \dfrac{1 + 6 + 9}{3\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{16}{3\sqrt{3}}$

Subtracting the lower limit value from the upper limit value:

$I = \dfrac{48}{3\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{16}{3\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{32}{3\sqrt{3}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{32}{3\sqrt{3}}$

or $\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)\left[{\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)}^{2} - 3\left(\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ - a\left[{a}^{2} - 3b\right] = 0$

or ${a}^{2} / b = 3$

36861.text: The number of real solutions of the equation \(x\left(x^2+3|x|+5|x-1|+6|x-2|\right)=0\) is ______.
36861.sol:

Given, $PQ = 4$ units and the distance between the points $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right) \text{ and } \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$ is $\sqrt{{\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ \sqrt{( \alpha - {2 )}^{2} + {\left(4 - \alpha\right)}^{2}} = 4$

$⇒ ( \alpha - {2 )}^{2} + {\left(4 - \alpha\right)}^{2} = {4}^{2}$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} - 4\alpha + 4 + 16 - 8\alpha + {\alpha}^{2} = 16$

If we take $\alpha = 3 - \sqrt{7},$ then $Q ≡ \left(3 - \sqrt{7}, 4 + \sqrt{7}\right)$

And, the slope of $PQ = m = \dfrac{4 + \sqrt{7} - 3}{3 - \sqrt{7} - 2} = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{7}}{1 - \sqrt{7}}$

37994.text: Let the equation of plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes $x + 2y + az = 2 and x - y + z = 3$ be $5x - 11y + bz = 6a - 1 .$ For $c \in \mathbb{Z},$ if the distance of this plane from the point $\left(a, - c, c\right)$ is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{a}},$ then $\dfrac{a + b}{c}$ is equal to
37994.sol:
Let the equation of plane passing through the intersection of two given planes:

$x + 2y + az - 2 + \lambda ( x - y + z - 3 ) = 0$

$⇒ x ( \lambda + 1 ) + y ( 2 - \lambda ) + z ( a + \lambda ) - 2 - 3\lambda = 0$

This is same as $5x - 11y + bz = 6a - 1$

$\dfrac{\lambda + 1}{5} = \dfrac{2 - \lambda}{- 11} = \dfrac{a + \lambda}{b} = \dfrac{2 + 3\lambda}{6a - 1}$

$⇒ - 11\lambda - 11 = 10 - 5\lambda$

$⇒ 6\lambda = - 21 ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{- 7}{2}$

$\dfrac{2 - \lambda}{- 11} = \dfrac{2 + 3\lambda}{6a - 1} ⇒ \dfrac{2 + \dfrac{7}{2}}{- 11} = \dfrac{2 - \dfrac{21}{2}}{6a - 1}$$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{- 17}{2 ( 6a - 1 )} ⇒ 6a - 1 = 17 ⇒ a = 3$

$\dfrac{2 - \lambda}{- 11} = \dfrac{a + \lambda}{b} ⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3 - \dfrac{7}{2}}{b}$

$⇒ - \dfrac{b}{2} = - \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ b = 1$

$∴$ point $( a, - c, c ) ≡ ( 3, - c, c )$

Distance$= \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{a}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

Plane$: 5x - 11y + z = 17$

The distance of the plane from $( 3, - c, c )$ is

$\left|\dfrac{15 + 11c + c - 17}{\sqrt{147}}\right| = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ | 12c - 2 | = 14$

$⇒ c = - 1, \dfrac{4}{3}$

$c = - 1\left(c \in \mathbb{Z}\right)$

$∴ \dfrac{a + b}{c} = \dfrac{3 + 1}{- 1} = - 4$

Hence this is the required option.

38333.text: If $n$ is the number of solutions of the equation $2cosx\left(4sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - x\right) - 1\right) = 1, x \in \left[0, \pi\right] and S$ is the sum of all these solutions, then the ordered pair $\left(n, S\right)$ is :
38333.sol:
$2cosx\left(4sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - x\right) - 1\right) = 1$

$⇒ 2cosx\left(2cos\left(2x\right) - 2cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 1\right) = 1$

$⇒ 2cosx\left(2 . \left(2\cos^{2}x - 1\right) - 1\right) = 1$

$⇒ 2cosx\left(4\cos^{2}x - 3\right) = 1$

$⇒ 4\cos^{3}x - 3cosx = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ cos3x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 3x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{5\pi}{3}, \dfrac{7\pi}{3}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{9}, \dfrac{5\pi}{9}, \dfrac{7\pi}{9}$

No. of solutions $= n = 3$

Sum of solutions $= S = \dfrac{\pi}{9} + \dfrac{5\pi}{9} + \dfrac{7\pi}{9} = \dfrac{13\pi}{9}$

38599.text: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three vectors such that $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) .$ If magnitudes of the vectors $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ are $\sqrt{2}, 1$ and $2$ respectively and the angle between $\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\theta\left(0 < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ then the value of $1 + tan\theta$ is equal to :
38599.sol:
We have, $\overset{\to}{a} = \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)\overset{\to}{b} - \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\overset{\to}{c}$

$= 1 . 2cos\theta\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = 2cos\theta\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}$

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = {\left|2cos\theta\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} - 2 . 2cos\theta\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = {\left(2cos\theta\right)}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} - 2 . 2cos\theta\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

Given that, $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 1$ and $\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 2$

${\left(\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(2cos\theta\right)}^{2} + {2}^{2} - 2 . 2cos\theta\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

$⇒ 2 = 4\cos^{2}\theta + 4 - 4cos\theta \cdot 2cos\theta$

$\left(∵ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|cos\theta\right)$

$⇒ - 2 = - 4\cos^{2}\theta$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$\left(∵ 0 < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Hence, $1 + tan\theta = 2 .$

by $S = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2}$

$⇒ 1 - \sqrt{3}\mu = \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} ⇒ \mu = \left(\dfrac{{\alpha}^{2} - 1}{{\alpha}^{2}}\right)\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ x = 3 . 00$

41080.sol:

Using ideal gas equation,

$PV = nRT$

We have, $P = $\dfrac{nRT}{V}

Putting$ in equation$\left(1\right),

$P{T}^{2} = $\dfrac{nRT}{V}$ \times {T}^{2} =$constant

$⇒ {T}^{3} = KV . . . $\left(2\right)$

Differentiating the equation with respect to $T$,

So, $\dfrac{d}{dT}\left(KV\right) = 3{T}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{KdV}{dT} = 3{T}^{2}$

$⇒ dV = \dfrac{3{T}^{2}}{K}dT$

$⇒ \gammaV = \dfrac{3{T}^{2}}{K}\left(\text{as}dV = \gammaVdT\right)$

$⇒ \gamma = \dfrac{3{T}^{2}}{KV} = \dfrac{3{T}^{2}}{{T}^{3}} = \dfrac{3}{T}$

$= 9.72$

42452.text: A small bob tied at one end of a thin string of length $1m$ is describing a vertical circle so that the maximum and minimum tension in the string is in the ratio $5: 1$. The velocity of the bob at the highest position is ______ $m{s}^{- 1}$. (Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
42452.sol:
Let the speed of bob at lowest position be ${v}_{1}$ and at the highest position be ${v}_{2}$.

Maximum tension is at lowest position and minimum tension is at the highest position.
Now, using, conservation of mechanical energy,

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2} + mg2l$

$⇒ {v}_{1}^{2} = {v}_{2}^{2} + 4gl . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now, ${T}_{max} - mg = \dfrac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l}$

$⇒ {T}_{max} = mg + \dfrac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l}$

$\text{ and } {T}_{min} + mg = \dfrac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l}$

$⇒ {T}_{min} = \dfrac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - mg$

$\dfrac{{T}_{max}}{{T}_{min}} = \dfrac{5}{1}$

43166.subject: Physics
43166.text: Two masses $m$ and 2 m are connected by a light string going over a pulley (disc) of mass 30 m with radius $r=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$. The pulley is mounted in a vertical plane and it is free to rotate about its axis. The 2 m mass is released from rest and its speed when it has descended through a height of 3.6 m is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$. (Assume string does not slip and $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$)
43166.sol:
Let the speed of the masses be $v$ and the angular velocity of the pulley be $\omega = v/r$ since the string does not slip.
The pulley is a disc of mass $M = 30m$ and radius $r$. Its moment of inertia is $I = \frac{1}{2}Mr^2 = \frac{1}{2}(30m)r^2 = 15mr^2$.
Using the principle of conservation of mechanical energy, the loss in potential energy of the system equals the gain in kinetic energy.
When the mass $2m$ descends by $h = 3.6$ m, the mass $m$ ascends by $h = 3.6$ m.
Loss in potential energy $\Delta U = (2m)gh - (m)gh = mgh$.
Gain in kinetic energy $\Delta K = \frac{1}{2}(2m)v^2 + \frac{1}{2}(m)v^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$.
Substituting $I$ and $\omega$: $\Delta K = \frac{3}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}(15mr^2)(\frac{v}{r})^2 = \frac{3}{2}mv^2 + \frac{15}{2}mv^2 = 9mv^2$.
Equating $\Delta U = \Delta K$: $mgh = 9mv^2$.
$v^2 = \frac{gh}{9}$.
Given $g = 10$ m/s$^2$ and $h = 3.6$ m:
$v^2 = \frac{10 \times 3.6}{9} = \frac{36}{9} = 4$.
$v = \sqrt{4} = 2$ m/s.

$⇒ \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {d}^{2}} - D = \dfrac{\lambda}{4}$

$⇒ {D}^{2} + {d}^{2} = {D}^{2} + \dfrac{{\lambda}^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{D\lambda}{2}$

$⇒ {d}^{2} = \dfrac{D\lambda}{2} + \dfrac{{\lambda}^{2}}{16}$

$⇒ {d}^{2} = \dfrac{0 . 2 \times 400 \times {10}^{- 9}}{2} + \dfrac{16 \times {10}^{- 14}}{16}$

$⇒ {d}^{2} \approx 400 \times {10}^{- 10}$

$\begin{cases}∴ d & = & 20 \times {10}^{- 5}m \\ & = & 0 . 20mm\end{cases}$

Therefore, $10\alpha = 2$.

44564.subject: Physics
44564.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: An object moves from position $r_{1}$ to position $r_{2}$ under a conservative force field $\vec{F}$. The work done by the force is $W=-\int_{r_{1}}^{r_{2}} \vec{F} \cdot \overrightarrow{d r}$.
Statement II: Any object moving from one location to another location can follow infinite number of paths. Therefore, the amount of work done by the object changes with the path it follows for a conservative force.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
44564.sol:
Statement I:
The work done by a force $\vec{F}$ during a displacement from $\vec{r}_1$ to $\vec{r}_2$ is defined as $W = \int_{r_1}^{r_2} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$.
The expression given in the statement, $W = -\int_{r_1}^{r_2} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$, is the definition of the change in potential energy ($\Delta U = -W$), not the work done by the force itself.
Thus, Statement I is false.

Statement II:
By definition, a conservative force is one for which the work done in moving an object between two points is independent of the path taken.
It only depends on the initial and final positions.
Therefore, the claim that work done changes with the path for a conservative force is false.

Since both statements are false, the correct option is (1).

49533.subject: Mathematics
49533.text: The angle between the lines whose direction ratios are $a, b, c$ and $b - c, c - a, a - b$ is
49533.sol:
Let the direction ratios of the two lines be represented by vectors $\vec{d_1}$ and $\vec{d_2}$.

$\vec{d_1} = a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + c\hat{k}$

$\vec{d_2} = (b - c)\hat{i} + (c - a)\hat{j} + (a - b)\hat{k}$

The angle $\theta$ between the lines is given by $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\vec{d_1} \cdot \vec{d_2}}{|\vec{d_1}| |\vec{d_2}|}$.

Calculating the dot product of the direction vectors:

$\vec{d_1} \cdot \vec{d_2} = a(b - c) + b(c - a) + c(a - b)$

$\vec{d_1} \cdot \vec{d_2} = ab - ac + bc - ab + ac - bc = 0$

Since the dot product is zero, the vectors are perpendicular.

$\cos\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \theta = 90^{}^{\circ}$

Answer: $90^{}^{\circ}$

52472.text: A planet of radius $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is revolving around a star of radius $\mathrm{R}^{*}$, which is at temperature $\mathrm{T}^{*}$. The distance between the star and the planet is $\mathrm{d}$. If the planet's temperature is $f \mathrm{ T}^{*}$, then $f$ is proportional to

The planet should be in Thermal equilibrium with star.

Amount of heat energy emitted by start per second $\mathrm{E}_{1}=\left(\sigma \mathrm{T}^{* 4}\right)\left(4 \pi \mathrm{R}^{*^{2}}\right)$
$\because \mathrm{d}=$ distance between star and planet
Hence, amount of energy reaching planet per
$\begin{aligned}

&=\frac{\left(\sigma \mathrm{T}^{* 4}\right)\left(4 \pi \mathrm{R}^{* 2}\right)}{4 \pi \mathrm{d}^{2}} \\
&=\frac{\sigma \mathrm{T}^{*^{4}} \mathrm{R}^{* 2}}{\mathrm{~d}^{2}}
\end{aligned}$
Hence energy received by planet per second
$\mathrm{E}_{2}=\left(\frac{\sigma \mathrm{T}^{* 4} \mathrm{R}^{* 2}}{\mathrm{~d}^{2}}\right) \pi \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{P}}^{2}$ $\mathrm{~T}=$ Temperature of planet then amount of energy emitted by planet per second
$$
E_{3}=\left(\sigma T^{4}\right)\left(4 \pi R_{P}^{2}\right)
$$
For thermal equilibrium $E_{3}=E_{2}$
$$
\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow\left(\sigma \mathrm{T}^{4}\right)\left(4 \pi \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{P}}^{2}\right)=\frac{\left(\sigma \mathrm{T}^{* 4} \mathrm{R}^{* 2}\right)}{\mathrm{d}^{2}}\left(\pi \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{p}}^{2}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}^{4}=\frac{\mathrm{T}^{* 4} \mathrm{R}^{* 2}}{4 \mathrm{~d}^{2}} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}=\mathrm{T}^{*} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{R}^{*}}{2 \mathrm{~d}}}=\mathrm{fT}^{*} \\

57757.subject: Chemistry
57757.text: When excess of chlorine is used in the chlorination of methane find the major product obtained.
57757.sol:
Chlorination of methane is a free radical substitution reaction.

When an excess of chlorine is used, all the hydrogen atoms of methane are successively replaced by chlorine atoms.

The sequence of reactions is:
$CH_4 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CH_3Cl + HCl$
$CH_3Cl + Cl_2 \rightarrow CH_2Cl_2 + HCl$
$CH_2Cl_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CHCl_3 + HCl$
$CHCl_3 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CCl_4 + HCl$

Thus, the final major product obtained is tetrachloromethane (CCl_4$).

Answer: Tetrachloromethane$

58247.subject: Chemistry
58247.text: Identify the correct decreasing order of boiling point for hydrides of halogens.
58247.sol:
The boiling points of hydrogen halides are determined by their intermolecular forces.

Hydrogen fluoride (HF) exhibits strong hydrogen bonding due to fluorine's high electronegativity and small size, resulting in a significantly elevated boiling point compared to other hydrogen halides.

Hydrogen chloride (HCl), hydrogen bromide (HBr), and hydrogen iodide (HI) lack hydrogen bonding capabilities. Their boiling points depend on London dispersion forces, which strengthen with increasing molecular size and electron count.

$\text{HI} > \text{HBr} > \text{HCl}$ due to HI's largest molecular size and highest electron count, producing the strongest London dispersion forces. HBr exhibits intermediate strength, while HCl has the weakest forces.

HF's hydrogen bonding gives it the highest boiling point, exceeding even HI's. The complete ordering is $\text{HF} > \text{HI} > \text{HBr} > \text{HCl}$.

This corresponds to option C.

58810.subject: Chemistry
58810.text: Calculate the number of atoms in 1 g metal that forms bcc crystal structure $[\rho \times a^3 = 6 \cdot 6 \times 10^{-22} \text{ g}]$
58810.sol:
The mass of one unit cell is given by the product of its density and volume:

Mass of unit cell $= \rho \times a^3 = 6 \cdot 6 \times 10^{-22} \text{ g}$

For a body-centered cubic (bcc) crystal structure, the number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 2$.

Mass of one atom $= \dfrac{\text{Mass of unit cell}}{Z} = \dfrac{6 \cdot 6 \times 10^{-22}}{2} = 3 \cdot 3 \times 10^{-22} \text{ g}$

The number of atoms in $1 \text{ g}$ of the metal is:

Number of atoms $= \dfrac{1 \text{ g}}{\text{Mass of one atom}} = \dfrac{1}{3 \cdot 3 \times 10^{-22}} = 3 \cdot 03 \times 10^{21}$

Answer: $3 \cdot 03 \times 10^{21}$

59147.subject: Chemistry
59147.text: Which from following mixtures obeys Raoult's law?
59147.sol:
Mixtures obeying Raoult's law form ideal solutions where intermolecular A-B interactions equal the average of A-A and B-B interactions, resulting in zero enthalpy (\Delta H_{mix} = 0$) and volume (\Delta V_{mix} = 0$) of mixing.

Phenol and aniline exhibit hydrogen bonding stronger than their pure components' interactions, causing negative deviation.

Chloroform and acetone form hydrogen bonds between chloroform's hydrogen and acetone's oxygen, also leading to negative deviation.

Ethanol and acetone experience disrupted hydrogen bonding in ethanol, weakening overall interactions and producing positive deviation.

Benzene and toluene, both non-polar aromatic hydrocarbons with similar London dispersion forces, maintain equivalent intermolecular interactions across the mixture, forming an ideal solution that obeys Raoult's law.

Amount of work done $= - ∆ nRT$
1 mole of methane reacts with 2 moles of oxygen to produce 2 moles of $C{O}_{2}$

$∴ {n}_{1} =$ moles of reactants = 1.5
${n}_{2} =$ moles of product = 1
$∴ ∆ n = {n}_{2} - {n}_{1} = 1 - 1.5 = - 0.5$

62733.text:
If $\mathrm{f}(x)= \begin{cases}\frac{8^x-4^x-2^x+1^x}{x^2} & , \text{ if } x > 0 \\ \mathrm{e}^x \sin x+i x+\lambda \log 4 & , \text{ if } x \leqslant 0, i \in \mathbb{R}\end{cases}$
is continuous at $x=0$, then the value of $500 e^\lambda$ is
62733.sol:
Ensuring continuity at $x=0$ requires:

$\lim_{x\to 0^-} \mathrm{f}(x) = \lim_{x\to 0^+} \mathrm{f}(x) = \mathrm{f}(0)$


The left-hand limit evaluates to $\lambda \log 4$, as $\mathrm{e}^x \to 1$, $\sin x \to 0$, and $i x \to 0$.


The right-hand limit transforms to $\lim_{x\to 0^+} \frac{(4^x-1)(2^x-1)}{x^2}$. Applying the standard limit $\lim_{x\to 0} \frac{a^x-1}{x} = \log a$ yields $(\log 4)(\log 2)$.


Since $\log 4 = 2\log 2$, this simplifies to $2(\log 2)^2$.


Equating both sides: $\lambda \log 4 = 2(\log 2)^2$. Substituting $\log 4 = 2\log 2$ gives $\lambda (2\log 2) = 2(\log 2)^2$, so $\lambda = \log 2$.


The expression $500\mathrme^{\lambda}$ becomes $500\mathrme^{\log 2} = 500 \cdot 2 = 1000$.


$\boxed{1000}$

Plane through intersection: $P_1 + \lambda P_2 = (2x - y + z - 3) + \lambda(4x - 3y + 5z + 9) = 0$

Rewriting: $(2 + 4\lambda)x + (-1 - 3\lambda)y + (1 + 5\lambda)z + (-3 + 9\lambda) = 0$

The plane is parallel to the line with direction vector $\vec{v} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$. The normal vector $\vec{n} = (2 + 4\lambda)\hat{i} + (-1 - 3\lambda)\hat{j} + (1 + 5\lambda)\hat{k}$ must be perpendicular to $\vec{v}$, so their dot product is zero:

$\vec{n} \cdot \vec{v} = (2 + 4\lambda)(2) + (-1 - 3\lambda)(4) + (1 + 5\lambda)(5) = 0$

Simplifying: $4 + 8\lambda - 4 - 12\lambda + 5 + 25\lambda = 0$
$5 + 21\lambda = 0$
$\lambda = -\frac{5}{21}$

Substitute back into the plane equation:
$(2 + 4(-\frac{5}{21}))x + (-1 - 3(-\frac{5}{21}))y + (1 + 5(-\frac{5}{21}))z + (-3 + 9(-\frac{5}{21})) = 0$
Simplifying: $\frac{22}{21}x - \frac{6}{21}y - \frac{4}{21}z - \frac{108}{21} = 0$
Multiply by 21: $22x - 6y - 4z - 108 = 0$

Simplify by dividing by 2: $11x - 3y - 2z - 54 = 0$

With $\alpha = 11$, $\beta = -3$, $\gamma = -2$, $d = -54$:
$\alpha + \beta + \gamma + d = 11 - 3 - 2 - 54 = -48$

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$

65070.subject: Mathematics
65070.text: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram ABCD are given by $\overline{AB} = 2\hat{i} + 10\hat{j} + 11\hat{k}$ and $\overline{AD} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. The side $AD$ is rotated by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram so that $AD$ becomes $AD'$. If $AD'$ makes a right angle with the side $AB$, then the cosine of the angle $\alpha$ is...
65070.sol:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$.

$\cos\theta = \dfrac{\overrightarrow{AB} \cdot \overrightarrow{AD}}{|\overrightarrow{AB}| |\overrightarrow{AD}|}$

Given $\overrightarrow{AB} = 2\hat{i} + 10\hat{j} + 11\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, we have:

$\overrightarrow{AB} \cdot \overrightarrow{AD} = (2)(-1) + (10)(2) + (11)(2) = -2 + 20 + 22 = 40$

$|\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 10^2 + 11^2} = \sqrt{4 + 100 + 121} = \sqrt{225} = 15$

$|\overrightarrow{AD}| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{9} = 3$

$\cos\theta = \dfrac{40}{15 \times 3} = \dfrac{40}{45} = \dfrac{8}{9}$

Since $\cos\theta > 0$, $\theta$ is an acute angle.

The vector $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is rotated by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram to become $\overrightarrow{AD'}$, which is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{AB}$. This means the angle between $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD'}$ is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Since all vectors lie in the same plane, the angle of rotation $\alpha$ is either $90^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta$ or $90^{{}^{\circ}} + \theta$. Because $\alpha$ is given as an acute angle, we must have:

$\alpha = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta$

Therefore, the cosine of the angle $\alpha$ is:

$\cos\alpha = \cos(90^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta) = \sin\theta$

Using the identity $\sin\theta = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2\theta}$ (since $\theta$ is acute):

$\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{8}{9}\right)^2} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{64}{81}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{17}{81}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$

65203.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are three vectors such that $\overline{|a|}=3, \overline{|b|}=5, \overline{|c|}=7$ then $|\bar{a}-\bar{b}|^2+|\bar{b}-\bar{c}|^2+|\bar{c}-\bar{a}|^2$ does not exceed
65203.sol:
Given vectors $\bar{a}$, $\bar{b}$, and $\bar{c}$ with magnitudes $|\bar{a}| = 3$, $|\bar{b}| = 5$, and $|\bar{c}| = 7$, we compute $E = |\bar{a}-\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{b}-\bar{c}|^2 + |\bar{c}-\bar{a}|^2$.

Using the identity $|\bar{x}-\bar{y}|^2 = |\bar{x}|^2 + |\bar{y}|^2 - 2\bar{x} \cdot \bar{y}$, we expand:

$E = (|\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 - 2\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) + (|\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2 - 2\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c}) + (|\bar{c}|^2 + |\bar{a}|^2 - 2\bar{c} \cdot \bar{a})$

Summing terms yields $E = 2(|\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2) - 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} + \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} + \bar{c} \cdot \bar{a})$.

With $|\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2 = 9 + 25 + 49 = 83$, we have $E = 166 - 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} + \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} + \bar{c} \cdot \bar{a})$.

From $|\bar{a}+\bar{b}+\bar{c}|^2 = |\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2 + 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} + \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} + \bar{c} \cdot \bar{a})$, we substitute:

$E = 2(83) - [|\bar{a}+\bar{b}+\bar{c}|^2 - 83] = 249 - |\bar{a}+\bar{b}+\bar{c}|^2$.

Since $|\bar{a}+\bar{b}+\bar{c}|^2 \geq 0$, $E$ is maximized when $|\bar{a}+\bar{b}+\bar{c}|^2$ is minimized. The minimum value of $0$ is attainable because the vectors with magnitudes $3$, $5$, and $7$ satisfy the triangle inequalities: $3+5 > 7$, $3+7 > 5$, and $5+7 > 3$, confirming that $\bar{a}+\bar{b}+\bar{c} = \bar{0}$ is possible.

Thus, $E_{\text\max} = 249 - 0 = 249$.

The maximum value is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

66032.text: In an oscillating LC circuit, the maximum charge on the capacitor is Q. When the energy is stored equally between the electric and magnetic fields, the charge on the capacitor becomes
66032.sol:
The total energy of the oscillating LC circuit is given by $U = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C}$

Let $q$ be the charge on the capacitor when the energy is equally shared between the electric and magnetic fields.

The electric energy stored in the capacitor at this instant is $U_E = \dfrac{q^2}{2C}$

Since the energy is equally divided between the electric and magnetic fields, the electric energy is half of the total energy:

$U_E = \dfrac{U}{2}$

$\dfrac{q^2}{2C} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{Q^2}{2C} \right)$

$q^2 = \dfrac{Q^2}{2}$

$q = \dfrac{Q}{\sqrt{2}}$

68155.subject: Physics
68155.text: The energy needed for breaking a liquid drop of radius ' $R$ ' into 216 droplets, each of radius ' $r$ ' is ' $x$ ' times TR ${ }^2$. The value of ' $x$ ' is [ $\mathrm{T}=$ surface tension of the liquid]
68155.sol:
The energy required to break a liquid drop into smaller droplets depends on the increase in surface area due to the surface tension, expressed as $E = T \times \Delta A$.

Volume conservation relates the radii of the large drop and the small droplets. Initially, the volume is $\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3$, and after breaking into 216 droplets of radius $r$, the total volume remains unchanged: $\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 216 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$. Simplifying, $R^3 = 216r^3$, so $R = 6r$ and $r = \frac{R}{6}$.

The initial surface area is $A_{\text{initial}} = 4\pi R^2$, while the total final surface area is $A_{\text{final}} = 216 \times 4\pi r^2$. Substituting for $r$: $A_{\text{final}} = 216 \times 4\pi \left(\frac{R}{6}\right)^2 = 216 \times 4\pi \times \frac{R^2}{36} = 6 \times 4\pi R^2 = 24\pi R^2$.

The change in surface area is $\Delta A = A_{\text{final}} - A_{\text{initial}} = 24\pi R^2 - 4\pi R^2 = 20\pi R^2$.

Thus, the energy required is $E = T \times 20\pi R^2$.

Comparing with the given expression $E = xTR^2$, it follows that $x = 20\pi$.

71001.text: Select the INCORRECT statement with respect to the respiratory system.
options: The oropharynx is a common passage for food and air.
Larynx contains vocal cords for producing sound.
The trachea is supported by 'C' shaped rings of cartilage.
The trachea is internally lined by simple squamous epithelium.
71001.sol:
The pharynx is the common passage for food and air, with the oropharynx being a part of it.

The larynx is a cartilaginous box which helps in sound production and is hence called the sound box.

The trachea is a straight tube extending up to the mid-thoracic cavity. The trachea, primary, secondary and tertiary bronchi, and initial bronchioles are supported by incomplete ('C' shaped) cartilaginous rings.

The trachea is internally lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, not simple squamous epithelium. Simple squamous epithelium is found in the walls of alveoli where it forms a diffusion boundary.

Answer: The trachea is internally lined by simple squamous epithelium.

71366.subject: Biology
71366.text:
Match List I with List II
List I
Types of gene interaction.		List II
Examples.
(A). Pleiotropy(I). Mirabilis jalapa
(B). Codominance(II). ABO blood group
(C). Incomplete dominance(III). Sickle cell anemia
(D). Multiple allele(IV). Coat color in cattle
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
71366.sol:
Pleiotropy occurs when a single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits. Sickle cell anemia is a classic example, where a single mutation in the beta-globin gene affects red blood cell shape, leading to multiple systemic effects.

Codominance is a condition where both alleles in a heterozygote are fully expressed. Coat color in cattle (roan coat) is an example, where both red and white hairs are expressed together.

Incomplete dominance occurs when the phenotype of the heterozygote is intermediate between the phenotypes of the homozygotes. Flower color in Mirabilis jalapa (Four o'clock plant) is an example, where a cross between red and white flowers produces pink flowers.

Multiple allelism refers to the presence of more than two alleles for a given gene within a population. The ABO blood group system in humans is an example, controlled by three alleles: $I^A$, $I^B$, and $i$.

Thus, the correct matching is (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)

71385.subject: Biology
71385.text: In a cross between a pure tall pea plant with yellow pod and a pure short plant with green pod, how many double recessive plants would you expect in $F_2$ generation?
71385.sol:
In pea plants, tallness (T$) is dominant over shortness (t$), and green pod colour (G$) is dominant over yellow pod colour (g$).

The cross is between a pure tall plant with yellow pods (TTgg$) and a pure short plant with green pods (ttGG$).

The $F_1$ generation will have the genotype $TtGg$, which corresponds to tall plants with green pods.

Upon selfing the $F_1$ generation (TtGg \times TtGg$), the $F_2$ generation is produced.

The phenotypic ratio of the $F_2$ generation in a dihybrid cross is 9:3:3:1$, which represents:
$9$ Tall, Green pods
$3$ Tall, Yellow pods
$3$ Short, Green pods
$1$ Short, Yellow pod

The double recessive phenotype is the short plant with yellow pods (ttgg$).

Out of 16$ possible combinations in the $F_2$ generation, only $1$ plant is double recessive.

Answer: One

71558.subject: Biology
71558.text:
Which of the following statements are correct about absorption of water in plants?
A. When water is absorbed by root hair cell its turgor pressure increases.
B. Its D.P.D. decreases.
C. The cortical cells immediately next to epiblema has more D. P. D.
D. A gradient of suction pressure develops from cells of the epiblema to the pericycle of the roots.
E. In roots, metaxylem is in close proximity with pericycle.
Choose the correct option given below.
options: A, B, C and D only
A, B, C and E only
B, C, D and E only.
A, C, D and E only
71558.sol:
When water is absorbed by a root hair cell, its turgor pressure (TP) increases due to the entry of water.

Diffusion Pressure Deficit (DPD) is given by DPD = OP - TP. As TP increases, the DPD of the cell decreases.

Water moves from a region of lower DPD to a region of higher DPD. For water to move from the root hair (epiblema) to the adjacent cortical cells, the cortical cells must have a higher DPD.

A continuous gradient of suction pressure (which is equivalent to DPD) is established from the epiblema to the pericycle, facilitating the inward radial movement of water.

In roots, the xylem is exarch, meaning the protoxylem lies towards the periphery and the metaxylem lies towards the center. Thus, the protoxylem is in close proximity to the pericycle, not the metaxylem. Statement E is incorrect.

Therefore, statements A, B, C, and D are correct.

Answer: A, B, C and D only

71629.text: Which of the following compounds will not undergo aldol condensation?
71629.sol:
Aldol condensation is given by aldehydes and ketones containing at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen atom.

Acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CHO}$) has three $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms.

Acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_3$) has six $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms.

Propionaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$) has two $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms.

Benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CHO}$) does not have any $\alpha$-hydrogen atom.

Therefore, benzaldehyde will not undergo aldol condensation.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CHO}$ (Benzaldehyde)

72078.subject: Physics
72078.text:
If the r.m.s. current in an a.c. circuit is $5$ A, having frequency $50$ Hz. The value of current $\dfrac{1}{300}$ s after its value becomes zero (in A) is
$\{\sin(\pi/3) = (3)^{0.5}/2\}$
72078.sol:
The equation for alternating current is given by $I = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$.

Given $I_{rms} = 5$ A, the peak current is:
$I_0 = I_{rms}\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}$ A

The angular frequency is:
$\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 50 = 100\pi$ rad/s

Substituting $t = \dfrac{1}{300}$ s into the current equation:
$I = 5\sqrt{2} \sin \lleft(100\pi \times \dfrac{1}{300}\right)$

$I = 5\sqrt{2} \sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

$I = 5\sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$I = 5\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$A

Answer: $5\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

72261.text: A circular coil having '$n$' turns, each of radius '$r$' carries a current '$I$'. The magnetic field at a distance $x = \sqrt{3}\,r$ from its center, along the axis of the coil, is $[\mu_0$ = permeability of free space$]$
72261.sol:
The magnetic field at a distance $x$ on the axis of a circular coil of radius $r$ with $n$ turns carrying current $I$ is given by

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(r^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

Given $x = \sqrt{3}r$, substituting this value into the formula:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(r^2 + (\sqrt{3}r)^2)^{3/2}}$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(r^2 + 3r^2)^{3/2}}$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(4r^2)^{3/2}}$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I r^2}{2(8r^3)}$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I}{16r}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\mu_0 nI}{16r}$

77033.subject: Mathematics
77033.text: What is the solution of the differential equation $\cos\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)=p$ when $y(0)=q$ ?
77033.sol:
The given differential equation is $\cos\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)=p$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos^{-1}(p)$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:

$y = x \cos^{-1}(p) + C$

Given $y(0) = q$, substituting $x = 0$ and $y = q$:

$q = 0 + C \Rightarrow C = q$

Substituting the value of $C$ in the equation:

$y = x \cos^{-1}(p) + q$

$\Rightarrow y - q = x \cos^{-1}(p)$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{y - q}{x} = \cos^{-1}(p)$

$\Rightarrow \cos\left(\dfrac{y - q}{x}\right) = p$

Answer: $\cos\left(\dfrac{y-q}{x}\right)=p$

77542.subject: Mathematics
77542.sol:
Let $\theta = \sec^{-1} \left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)

\Rightarrow \sec \theta = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}

⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}

The given expression becomes \tan \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \theta\right) = \tan \left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)

\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right) = \tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \tan(45^{{}^{\circ}} - 30^{{}^{\circ}})$

Using the formula $\tan(A - B) = \dfrac{\tan A - \tan B}{1 + \tan A \tan B}

\tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \dfrac{\tan 45^{{}^{\circ}} - \tan 30^{{}^{\circ}}}{1 + \tan 45^{{}^{\circ}} \tan 30^{{}^{\circ}}}

\tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1}

Rationalizing the denominator:

\tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \dfrac{(\sqrt{3} - 1)^2}{(\sqrt{3} + 1)(\sqrt{3} - 1)} = \dfrac{3 + 1 - 2\sqrt{3}}{3 - 1}

\tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \dfrac{4 - 2\sqrt{3}}{2} =2 - \sqrt{3}

Answer: 2 - \sqrt{3}$

77865.subject: Mathematics
77865.text: Let $n$ be a natural number. The number of consecutive zeros at the end of the expansion of $n!$ is exactly 2. How many values of $n$ are possible?
77865.sol:
The number of consecutive zeros at the end of $n!$ is determined by the exponent of $5$ in the prime factorization of $n!$.

Using Legendre's formula, the exponent of $5 in n!$ is given by:

$E_5(n!) = \left\lfloor \dfrac{n}{5} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \dfrac{n}{5^2} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \dfrac{n}{5^3} \right\rfloor + \dots$

Given that $E_5(n!) = 2$, $n$ must be less than $25$, which means $\left\lfloor \dfrac{n}{25} \right\rfloor = 0$ and all higher terms are also $0$.

Thus, the equation simplifies to:

$\left\lfloor \dfrac{n}{5} \right\rfloor = 2$

This inequality holds for:

$2 \le \dfrac{n}{5} \lt 3$

$10 \le n \lt 15$

Since $n$ is a natural number, the possible values of $n$ are $10, 11, 12, 13, 14$.

There are exactly $5$ possible values for $n$.

Answer: $5$

78414.text: In an $A P$, the ratio of the sum of the first $p$ terms to the sum of the first $q$ terms is $p^2: q^2$. Which one of the following is correct?
options: The first term is equal to the common difference
The first term is equal to twice the common difference
The common difference is equal to twice the first term
The first term is equal to square of the common difference
78414.sol:
$We have,
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{S_p}{S_q}=\frac{p^2}{q^2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\frac{p}{2}[2 a+(p-1) d]}{\frac{q}{2}[2 a+(q-1) d]}=\frac{p^2}{q^2}\left\{\because S_n=\frac{n}{2}[2 a+(n-1) d]\right\} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2 a+(p-1) d}{2 a+(q-1) d}=\frac{p}{q} \\
& \Rightarrow 2 a q+q(p-1) d=2 a p+p(q-1) d \\
& \Rightarrow 2 a(q-p)=d(q-p) \\
& \Rightarrow 2 a=d \text{$ or $} d=2 a
\end{aligned}$
This, the common difference is equal to twice of the first term.

81266.text: Although $+3$ oxidation state is most common in lanthanoids, cerium still shows $+4$ oxidation state because :

The atomic number of Cerium (Ce) is $58$.

The electronic configuration of Ce is $[Xe] 4f^{1} 5d^{1} 6s^{2}$.

In $+3$ oxidation state, the electronic configuration of $Ce^{3+}$ is $[Xe] 4f^{1}$.

By losing one more electron, it forms $Ce^{4+}$ ion.

The electronic configuration of $Ce^{4+}$ is $[Xe] 4f^{0}$, which is a highly stable noble gas configuration.

Thus, Cerium shows $+4$ oxidation state because after losing one more electron from $+3$ state, it acquires $4f^{0}$ electronic configuration.

82688.subject: Physics
82688.text: Two metal spheres, one of radius $\mathrm{R}$ and the other of radius $2 \mathrm{R}$ respectively have the same surface charge density $\sigma$. They are brought in contact and separated. What will be the new surface charge densities on them?
82688.sol:
The surface charge density of a closed surface area having charge $\mathrm{Q}$ is given by $$ \sigma=\frac{\text{ Charge }}{\text{ Area }}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{A}} \text{ or } \mathrm{Q}=\sigma \mathrm{A} $$ Thus, the charges on sphere P and Q having same charge density as shown in the figure below is given by
$$ \begin{gathered} \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{P}}=\sigma \times 4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2=4 \pi \sigma \mathrm{R}^2 \\ \text{ and } \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{Q}}=\sigma \times 4 \pi(2 \mathrm{R})^2=16 \pi \sigma \mathrm{R}^2 \end{gathered} $$ when they are brought in contact with each other, the total charge will be $$ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{t}} & =\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{P}}+\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{Q}} \\ = & 4 \pi \sigma \mathrm{R}^2+16 \pi \sigma \mathrm{R}^2 \text{ [From Eq. (i) and (ii)] } \\ & =20 \pi \sigma \mathrm{R}^2 \end{aligned} $$ In connection of two charged conducting bodies, the potential will become same on both, i.e. $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{P}}}{4 \pi \in_0 \mathrm{R}}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{Q}}}{4 \pi \epsilon_0 2 \mathrm{R}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{Q}}}{2 \mathrm{R}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{Q}}}=\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned} $$ So, the charges on the sphere $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ after separation will be distributed as $$ \Rightarrow \quad Q_P^{\prime}=\frac{1}{3} Q_{\mathrm{t}} \text{ and } \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{Q}}^{\prime}=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{t}} $$ After separation, the new surface charge densities on $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ will be $$ \begin{aligned} \sigma_{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{P}}^{\prime}}{\text{ Area }} & =\frac{1}{3} \frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\text{ Area }}=\frac{1}{3} \frac{20 \pi \sigma \mathrm{R}^2}{4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2}=\frac{5}{3} \sigma \\ \text{ and } \sigma_{\mathrm{Q}}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{Q}}^{\prime}}{\text{ Area }} & =\frac{2}{3} \frac{\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\text{ Area }}=\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{20 \pi \sigma \mathrm{R}^2}{4 \pi(2 \mathrm{R})^2} \\ & =\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{5}{4} \sigma=\frac{5}{6} \sigma \end{aligned} $$

83885.subject: Zoology
83885.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : In recombinant DNA technology, lysozyme is used for disrupting bacterial cells while cellulase is for plant cells.
Reason R : Isolation of genetic material needs disruption of cells.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: $\text{A}$ is not correct but $\text{R}$ is correct
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct but $\text{R}$ is not the correct explanation of $\text{A}$
$\text{A}$ is correct but $\text{R}$ is not correct
83885.sol:
Assertion A is a correct statement. In recombinant DNA technology, bacterial cells are treated with the enzyme lysozyme to degrade their peptidoglycan cell walls, while plant cells are treated with cellulase to degrade their cellulosic cell walls.

Reason R is also a correct statement. The isolation of genetic material requires the disruption of the cell to release DNA along with other macromolecules like RNA, proteins, polysaccharides, and lipids.

However, Reason R does not explain the specificity of the enzymes mentioned in Assertion A. The correct explanation for Assertion A would be the difference in the biochemical composition of the cell walls of bacteria and plants. Therefore, both Assertion A and Reason R are correct, but Reason R is not the correct explanation of Assertion A.

101180.subject: Physics
101180.text: The angular momentum of a moving rigid body is measured about several different stationary points in the laboratory frame. It is found that the angular momentum vector is exactly the same about every point. Which of the following statements must be true regarding the motion of the body?
options: The body is undergoing pure translational motion with a constant velocity.
The body is rolling without slipping on a fixed horizontal surface.
The center of mass of the body is stationary.
The body is rotating about a fixed axis that does not pass through its center of mass.
101180.sol:
The angular momentum of a rigid body about any arbitrary stationary point $P$ is given by the relation:

$\vec{L}_P = \vec{L}_{cm} + \vec{r}_{cm/P} \times M\vec{v}_{cm}$

where $\vec{L}_{cm}$ is the angular momentum about the center of mass, $\vec{r}_{cm/P}$ is the position vector of the center of mass with respect to point $P$, $M$ is the mass, and $\vec{v}_{cm}$ is the velocity of the center of mass.

For the angular momentum $\vec{L}_P$ to be exactly the same about every stationary point $P$, the term $\vec{r}_{cm/P} \times M\vec{v}_{cm}$ must be zero for all possible position vectors $\vec{r}_{cm/P}$.

This is only possible if the velocity of the center of mass is zero ($\vec{v}_{cm} = 0$).

Therefore, the center of mass of the body must be stationary. The body can either be completely at rest or in pure rotation about an axis passing through its center of mass.

Answer: The center of mass of the body is stationary.

101248.subject: Physics
101248.text: Find ratio of radius of gyration of a disk and ring of same radii at their tangential axis in plane.
101248.sol:
For disk, moment of inertia about the diameter, $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{4}$ and moment of inertia about the tangential axis
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}_{\text{disc }}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}+\mathrm{mr}^2 \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\text{disc }}=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{4}+\mathrm{mr}^2 \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\text{disc }}=\frac{5 \mathrm{mr}^2}{4}\end{aligned}$
Let the radius of gyration of disc is $\mathrm{k}_{\text{disc }}$.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_{\text{disc }} & =\mathrm{mk}_{\text{disc }}^2 \\ \frac{5 \mathrm{mr}^2}{4} & =\mathrm{mk}_{\text{disc }}^2 \\ \mathrm{k}_{\text{disc }}^2 & =\sqrt{\frac{5}{4} \mathrm{r}}\end{aligned}$
For ring, moment of inertia about the diameter
$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{a}}^{\prime}=\mathrm{mr}^2 / 2$
and moment of inertia about the tangential axis
$\mathrm{I}_{\text{ring }}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{a}}^{\prime}+\mathrm{mr}^2=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2}+\mathrm{mr}^2=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mr}^2$
Let the radius of gyration of ring $\mathrm{k}_{\text{ring }}$.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_{\text{ring }} & =\mathrm{mk}^2 \text{ ring } \\ \frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mr}^2 & =\mathrm{mk}^2 \text{ ring } \\ \mathrm{k}_{\text{ring }} & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \mathrm{r} \\ \frac{\mathrm{k}_{\text{disc }}}{\mathrm{k}_{\text{ring }}} & =\frac{\sqrt{\frac{5}{4} \mathrm{r}}}{\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \mathrm{r}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}}\end{aligned}$

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
102414.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: The function $f(t) = \sin(\omega t) + \sin(2\omega t)$ is a superposition of two simple harmonic motions with angular frequencies $\omega$ and $2\omega$. Since the ratio of their frequencies is a rational number, their sum repeats after a definite time interval and is therefore periodic. However, because the frequencies are different, the resulting motion is not a simple harmonic motion.

Reason (R) is false: A function represents simple harmonic motion only if it can be expressed as a single sine or cosine function, such as $A \sin(\omega' t + \phi)$. The given function $f(t) = \sin(\omega t) + \sin(2\omega t)$ cannot be mathematically reduced to this form because the two terms have different angular frequencies.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

103315.sol:
Since the three batteries are connected in series and aid each other, the net EMF of the circuit is the sum of their individual EMFs.

$E_{\text{net}} = 5\text{ V} + 3\text{ V} + E = (8 + E)\text{ V}$

$I = \dfrac{E_{\text{net}}}{R_{\text{total}}}$

Substituting the given values:

$3 = \dfrac{8 + E}{4}$

$12 = 8 + E$

$E = 4\text{ V}$

Answer: $4\text{ V}$

104127.subject: Physics
104127.text:
Assertion: In a series LCR circuit, if the rms voltages across the inductor, capacitor, and resistor are $60\text{ V}$, $20\text{ V}$, and $30\text{ V}$ respectively, the peak voltage of the AC source is $50\sqrt{2}\text{ V}$.
Reason: The voltages across the inductor and capacitor are out of phase by $\pi$ radians, and their resultant is out of phase with the resistor's voltage by $\pi/2$ radians.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
104127.sol:
Assertion: The rms voltage of the source is found using phasor addition:
$V_{rms} = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$
$V_{rms} = \sqrt{30^2 + (60 - 20)^2} = \sqrt{900 + 1600} = 50\text{ V}$
The peak voltage of the source is $V_0 = V_{rms}\sqrt{2} = 50\sqrt{2}\text{ V}$. Thus, the Assertion is true.

Reason: In a series LCR circuit, the voltage across the inductor ($V_L$) leads the current by $\pi/2$, while the voltage across the capacitor ($V_C$) lags the current by $\pi/2$. Therefore, $V_L$ and $V_C$ are exactly $\pi$ radians ($180^\circ$) out of phase. Their resultant, $V_L - V_C$, is either leading or lagging the current by $\pi/2$. Since the voltage across the resistor ($V_R$) is in phase with the current, the resultant of the reactive components is out of phase with $V_R$ by $\pi/2$ radians ($90^\circ$). This perpendicular phase relationship is the exact reason why the voltages are added vectorially using the Pythagorean theorem to find the source voltage. Thus, the Reason is true and correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

105282.subject: Physics
105282.text: A $9.7\text{ V}$ DC battery is connected across a circuit that consists of three components in series: a $2\ \Omega$ resistor, a silicon diode, and a parallel combination of two resistors ($6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$). The diode is oriented such that it is forward-biased. If the silicon diode has a barrier potential of $0.7\text{ V}$ and a forward resistance of $0.5\ \Omega$, the total current drawn from the battery is:
105282.sol:
The circuit consists of a $2\ \Omega$ resistor, a forward-biased silicon diode, and a parallel combination of $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ resistors, all in series.

First, calculate the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination ($R_p$):
$R_p = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{6 + 3} = \dfrac{18}{9} = 2\ \Omega$

The silicon diode is non-ideal, so it has a barrier potential ($V_k = 0.7\text{ V}$) and a forward resistance ($r_f = 0.5\ \Omega$).

The total equivalent resistance of the circuit ($R_{eq}$) includes the series resistor, the diode's forward resistance, and the parallel combination:
$R_{eq} = R_1 + r_f + R_p = 2 + 0.5 + 2 = 4.5\ \Omega$

The effective voltage ($V_{eff}$) driving the current is the battery voltage minus the diode's barrier potential:
$V_{eff} = V - V_k = 9.7 - 0.7 = 9.0\text{ V}$

Using Ohm's law, the total current ($I$) is:
$I = \dfrac{V_{eff}}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{9.0}{4.5} = 2.0\text{ A}$

Answer: $2.00\text{ A}$

105552.subject: Physics
105552.text: Light of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on a photosensitive surface with a work function $W > 0$. The fastest emitted photoelectron has a de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_1$. When the incident wavelength is changed to $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$, the fastest photoelectron has a de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_2$. Which of the following inequalities correctly relates $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$?
105552.sol:
From Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy for the initial wavelength $\lambda$ is:
$K_1 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - W$

When the incident wavelength is halved to $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$, the new maximum kinetic energy is:
$K_2 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda/2} - W = \dfrac{2hc}{\lambda} - W$

We can express $K_2$ in terms of $K_1$:
$K_2 = 2\left(K_1 + W\right) - W = 2K_1 + W$

Since the work function $W > 0$, it follows that $K_2 > 2K_1$.

The de-Broglie wavelength is inversely proportional to the square root of the kinetic energy ($\lambda_d = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$).

Therefore, for the new wavelength:
$\lambda_2 = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK_2}}$

Since $K_2 > 2K_1$, we have:
$\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK_2}} < \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m(2K_1)}}$

$\lambda_2 < \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \left(\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK_1}}\right)$

$\lambda_2 < \dfrac{\lambda_1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Answer: $\lambda_2 < \dfrac{\lambda_1}{\sqrt{2}}$

107787.subject: Chemistry
107787.text: Which of the following molecules has a zero dipole moment?
107787.sol:
Dipole moment is a vector quantity and depends on the molecular geometry.

In $\mathrm{BeF}_2$, the central beryllium atom has no lone pairs and forms two sigma bonds. It has a linear geometry. The two Be-F bond dipoles are equal and point in opposite directions, cancelling each other out to give a net zero dipole moment.

$\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ has a bent shape due to two lone pairs on oxygen, so its bond dipoles do not cancel.

$\mathrm{NH}_3$ has a trigonal pyramidal shape due to one lone pair on nitrogen, resulting in a non-zero net dipole moment.

$\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$ has a tetrahedral geometry, but since the four substituents are not identical, the individual bond dipoles do not cancel out completely.

Answer: $\mathrm{BeF}_2$

Substituting these values into the equation:

$-400\text{ J} = q + 150\text{ J}$

$q = -400\text{ J} - 150\text{ J} = -550\text{ J}$

The negative sign indicates that $550\text{ J}$ of heat is released by the system.

Answer: $550\text{ J}$ released

114890.subject: Chemistry
114890.text: A first-order reaction takes $46.06\text{ minutes}$ to reach $99\%$ completion. The rate constant of the reaction is :
114890.sol:
For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate law is given by:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}$

Let the initial concentration $[A]_0$ be $100$. For $99\%$ completion, the remaining concentration $[A]_t$ is $100 - 99 = 1$.

Substituting the given values:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{46.06} \log \dfrac{100}{1}$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{46.06} \times 2$

$k = \dfrac{4.606}{46.06}$

$k = 0.1\text{ min}^{-1}$

Answer: $0.1\text{ min}^{-1}$

115310.subject: Chemistry
115310.text:
Out of the following :-
(A) Argyrol - eye lotion
(B) Colloidal antimony - Stomach disorder.
(C) Colloidal gold - Kalaazar
(D) Milk of magnesia - Skin disease
(E) Colloidal Sulphur - Intramuscular injection.
The correct one is :-
115310.sol:
(A) Argyrol - eye lotion
- Correct. Argyrol is a colloidal silver preparation used as an antiseptic eye lotion.
(B) Colloidal antimony - Stomach disorder.
- Incorrect. Colloidal antimony is primarily used in the treatment of leishmaniasis (Kalaazar), not for stomach disorders.
(C) Colloidal gold - Kalaazar
- Incorrect. Colloidal gold is not typically used for Kalaazar; instead, colloidal antimony (e.g., Sodium stibogluconate) is used for this purpose.
(D) Milk of magnesia - Skin disease
- Incorrect. Milk of magnesia (magnesium hydroxide) is primarily used as an antacid or laxative, not specifically for skin diseases.
(E) Colloidal Sulphur - Intramuscular injection.
- Incorrect. Colloidal sulfur is more commonly used in topical treatments for skin conditions such as acne and dandruff rather than as an intramuscular injection.
Based on this analysis, the correct option is:
(3) Only A.

Consider the following sequence of reactions:

Benzene reacts with oleum (fuming sulfuric acid) to undergo sulfonation, forming benzenesulfonic acid (Compound A).

121119.text: In what language are biological names generally written?
121119.sol: This system of providing a name with two components is called Binomial nomenclature. This naming system given by Carolus Linnaeus is being practised by biologists all over the world. This naming system using a two word format was found convenient. Let us take the example of mango to understand the way of providing scientific names better. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas. They occur in both well-lighted regions close to the surface of water and also at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates.The red thalli of most of the red algae are multicellular. The food is stored as floridean starch which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure. <mark>The red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation.</mark> They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes. 125951.text: What variation exists in the number of free nuclei before cellularization occurs?

125951.sol: Endosperm development precedes embryo development. Why? The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue. The cells of this tissue are filled with reserve food materials and are used for the nutrition of the developing embryo. In the most common type of endosperm development, the PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei. This stage of endosperm development is called free-nuclear endosperm. Subsequently cell wall formation occurs and the endosperm becomes cellular. The number of free nuclei formed before cellularisation varies greatly. 126241.subject: Botany
126241.text: A male plant with a diploid chromosome number of $16$ is crossed with a female plant that is tetraploid ($4n = 32$). What will be the exact number of chromosomes in the zygote and the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) of the resulting seed, respectively?
126241.sol:
The ploidy of the gametes depends on the ploidy of the parent plant.

The male plant is diploid ($2n = 16$), so its male gametes will be haploid ($n = 8$).

The female plant is tetraploid ($4n = 32$), so its gametes and the nuclei of the embryo sac will be diploid ($2n = 16$). Thus, the egg cell has $16$ chromosomes, and the central cell contains two polar nuclei, each with $16$ chromosomes.

During syngamy, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form the zygote:
Zygote = Male gamete ($8$) + Egg cell ($16$) = $24$ chromosomes.

During triple fusion, the second male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN):
PEN = Male gamete ($8$) + Polar nucleus 1 ($16$) + Polar nucleus 2 ($16$) = $40$ chromosomes.

Answer: $24$ and $40$

126248.subject: Botany
126248.text: Which of the following plants strictly exhibits the type of pollination that brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma?
126248.sol:
The type of pollination that brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma is xenogamy.

For a plant to strictly exhibit xenogamy and prevent both autogamy and geitonogamy, it must be dioecious (bearing male and female flowers on separate plants). Papaya is a dioecious plant, ensuring only xenogamy occurs.

Castor and maize are monoecious plants (bearing both male and female flowers on the same plant), which prevents autogamy but allows geitonogamy. Pea is a bisexual plant that naturally undergoes self-pollination (autogamy).

Answer: Papaya

128588.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the hormones of the menstrual cycle and their primary associated events or phases.

List-I (Hormones)List-II (Events/Phases)
A. LHI. Secretory phase
B. FSHII. Ovulation
C. EstrogenIII. Proliferative phase
D. ProgesteroneIV. Follicular development

128588.sol:
Luteinizing Hormone (LH) reaches its peak level during the mid-cycle (LH surge), which induces the rupture of the Graafian follicle and causes ovulation (A matches with II).

Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) stimulates the growth and development of the primary follicles into mature follicles (B matches with IV).

Estrogen, secreted by the growing follicles, stimulates the regeneration of the endometrium through proliferation, marking the proliferative phase (C matches with III).

Progesterone is secreted by the corpus luteum after ovulation and is essential for the maintenance of the endometrium during the secretory phase (D matches with I).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

128593.text: Which of the following correctly represents a structural polysaccharide, its monomeric unit, and the primary bond linking its monomers?
128593.sol:
Chitin is a structural polysaccharide found in the exoskeletons of arthropods and cell walls of fungi. It is a homopolymer of N-acetyl glucosamine (NAG) monomers linked by glycosidic bonds.

Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide, but its monomer is glucose, not fructose.

Glycogen is a homopolymer of glucose with glycosidic bonds, but it functions as a storage polysaccharide in animals, not a structural one.

Although chitin contains nitrogen in its modified sugar monomers, the monomers themselves are linked by glycosidic bonds, not peptide bonds.

Answer: Chitin - N-acetyl glucosamine - Glycosidic bond
